production.waterSource: The distillery uses pure water from the Lake District National Park in whisky production.
production.malt: Unpeated malted barley is used for The Lakes single malt.
production.fermentation: Three different yeast strains are combined to build layered flavour. Fermentation is extended to as much as 96 hours, deliberately reaching malolactic fermentation to increase complexity and creamy texture.
production.stills: The distillery uses copper pot distillation with separate wash and spirit stills. Distillation is run slowly to maximise copper contact and retain a robust, fruity spirit suited to active maturation.
production.maturation: The house philosophy is explicitly sherry-led and wood-forward. The distillery has expanded racked warehousing on site to support maturation and stock growth.

houseCharacter: The Lakes begins with unpeated malt and intentionally long, multi-yeast fermentation to create a robust, fruity and textural wash. Slow copper-pot distillation maximises copper contact while preserving enough body for active wood influence. The resulting spirit is engineered specifically for a sherry-led, wood-forward maturation regime rather than for neutral cask treatment.
cask23Narrative: The Lakes Distillery designs its spirit with maturation already in mind. Three yeast strains and fermentation of up to 96 hours build fruit and texture before slow copper distillation creates a spirit strong enough to stand up to assertive sherry-led wood. It is a useful example of modern English whisky making where fermentation, distillation and cask design are treated as one connected flavour system.
